category_fits.label: Consumer Behavior & Insights
category_fits.why_fit: The report is based on consumer research into online shopping adoption, retailer discovery, new-retailer use, delivery and pickup preferences, paid memberships, and data-sharing willingness.
category_fits.why_not_fit: The findings have retail implications, but the report's central lens is what shoppers do and expect, rather than retailer performance.

category_fits.label: Amazon Marketplace & Advertising
category_fits.why_fit: Explicit configured category evidence is central to the retained report context.
supported_topic_rules: Amazon retail, Amazon Ads, seller operations, or Amazon-specific planning decisions are central across the report.

category_fits.label: Beauty
category_fits.why_fit: Explicit configured category evidence is central to the retained report context.
supported_topic_rules: Evidence repeatedly discusses beauty products, beauty shoppers, personal care routines, or beauty category trends.

category_fits.label: Macroeconomics & Regional Outlooks
category_fits.why_fit: Explicit configured category evidence is central to the retained report context.
supported_topic_rules: The report interprets markets primarily through economy-wide forces rather than one product category or channel.

category_fits.label: Technology & Innovation
category_fits.why_fit: Explicit configured category evidence is central to the retained report context.
supported_topic_rules: Evidence repeatedly discusses infrastructure, enterprise technology, robotics, cybersecurity, hardware, or major technology shifts.

category_fits.label: Omnichannel Commerce
category_fits.why_fit: The report covers online shopping alongside fulfillment choices such as curbside and in-store pickup, and notes that car shoppers move discovery and consideration online.
category_fits.why_not_fit: It does not center on integration between online and physical touchpoints or end-to-end cross-touchpoint experience design; most findings concern online shopping behavior.

category_fits.label: Retail Logistics & Fulfillment
category_fits.why_fit: A section compares the fulfillment options consumers most frequently use, including delivery, curbside pickup, and in-store pickup.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Fulfillment is one part of a broader report on shopper behavior; inventory, warehousing, last-mile operations, and execution complexity are not the central focus.
supported_topic_rules: Evidence centers on how inventory, delivery, fulfillment, or returns drive performance and shopper experience.

category_fits.label: eGrocery
category_fits.why_fit: The report includes online grocery adoption, retailer starting points, new retailer use, and grocery delivery and pickup preferences.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Grocery is one of several product categories studied; the report also covers clothing, beauty/grooming, and car shopping, so grocery is not the core commercial context.
supported_topic_rules: Evidence repeatedly covers grocery ecommerce, delivery windows, basket missions, rapid fulfillment, or grocery-specific digital adoption.
rejected_topic_rules: Reject when grocery appears only as one product category inside a broader retail or FMCG report.

category_fits.label: Online Marketplaces & Platforms
category_fits.why_fit: The report mentions Amazon and other retailer websites or apps as places where shoppers begin online shopping.
category_fits.why_not_fit: It reports shopper starting points and discovery habits, not marketplace economics, seller acquisition, buyer-seller dynamics, or platform growth strategy.

category_fits.label: Privacy, Identity & Data
category_fits.why_fit: The overview says the report considers consumers' willingness to share data for personalized or monetary benefits.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Data sharing is one topic within a broad online-shopping study; the context does not describe privacy, consent, identity resolution, compliance, or data collaboration as the report's core problem.

category_fits.label: Fashion
category_fits.why_fit: The report includes clothing online penetration and where online clothing shoppers typically start.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Clothing is one category in a broader study of post-COVID online shopping; the report does not focus on apparel, fashion demand, merchandising, or fashion retail dynamics.
